events.title: Devotional: Elder Neil L. Andersen
events.description:
Elder Neil L. Andersen was named an Apostle of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on April 4, 2009. Elder Andersen was serving as the senior member of the Presidency of the Seventy prior to his calling to the Quorum of the Twelve. He was named a member of the First Quorum of the Seventy in April 1993, at age 41. He previously led the work of the Church in southern Brazil and, again as a member of an area presidency, oversaw the Church in Western Europe. Prior to his call as a General Authority, Elder Andersen served as a mission president in the France Bordeaux Mission and as president of the Tampa Florida Stake.

He graduated from BYU, where he was a Hinckley Scholar, and he earned a Master of Business Administration from Harvard University.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

He developed a record of success as a senior leader and manager of interagency teams to advance US strategic priorities and as a strategist and negotiator. His senior positions included Ambassador to Kosovo and Chargé d’Affaires and Deputy Chief of Mission in Turkey. He also served as Acting Deputy Chief of Mission and Minister Counselor for Political Affairs at the US Embassy to Germany; at embassies in Peru, Greece, Croatia, Paraguay, and Panama; and at the US Mission to the OSCE.

Greer believes our future depends on our ability to talk to each other across our differences.

Artemis II marked America’s return to the Moon after more than fifty years, serving as a powerful symbol of national ambition and collective effort. Ultimately, Artemis II reminded Americans of their capacity to work together toward ambitious goals and inspired a renewed sense of shared purpose.

events.title: The Role of Faith in Human Flourishing
events.description:
What does it truly mean to flourish—and how can societies help people achieve it?

Drawing on groundbreaking data, Dr. Byron Johnson, Director of the Institute for Global Human Flourishing at Baylor University, will explore the links between faith, well-being, and human flourishing, revealing surprising insights about purpose, relationships, and the pathways to a thriving life. The event will be held at 7pm in the Hinckley Center Assembly Hall at Brigham Young University, serving as the opening keynote address of the Religion and Human Flourishing conference.

This lecture is co-sponsored by Wheatley Institute, Brigham Young University's College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences, and College of Religious Education.

ABOUT THE SPEAKER:

Dr. Byron Johnson is the Director of the Institute for Global Human Flourishing at Baylor University. He is the author of more than 350 journal articles, monographs, and books, focusing much of his professional career on the scientific study of religion, the efficacy of faith-based organizations, and criminal justice. Dr. Johnson is also the project co-director of the Global Flourishing Study. The multi-year data collection and research collaboration has brought researchers from Baylor and Harvard University in partnership with Gallup and the Center for Open Science to gather data from approximately 200,000 participants from 22 countries in order to create an open access resource for researchers, journalists, policymakers, and educators worldwide.

events.title: Deep Roots, Open Arms: Truman G. Madsen Lecture on Eternal Man
events.description:
Must we choose between the security of deep roots — a particular faith, culture, or community that knows its own — and the openness of hospitality toward those who differ from us? Anne Snyder, editor-in-chief of Comment magazine, argues this is a false choice. Drawing on some of America's most generative religious and civic traditions, she explores how our most rooted communities can become schools of hospitality — forming people capable of loving what is distinctly their own while still reaching beyond it.

Her lecture, which represents the 2026 Truman G. Madsen Lecture on Eternal Man, will be held in the Assembly Hall at the Hinckley Center at Brigham Young University.

BYU Professor Truman G. Madsen was a renowned philosopher, teacher, and biographer and is regarded as one of the great thinkers within the Latter-day Saint tradition. One of his goals as a founding senior fellow of Wheatley Institute was to bring academic experts and thought leaders “to the fire” at Brigham Young University. In honor of this goal, the Madsen Lecture brings leading scholars of faith from across the spectrum of religious traditions to BYU and provides them an opportunity to discuss their work on the foundational relationship between faith and reason.

Bishop Budge was sustained as a General Authority Seventy on April 6, 2019, and served in that capacity until his call as Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric in October 2020. Bishop Budge has served in a number of Church callings, including stake president, president of the Japan Tokyo Mission, and Area Seventy.

Bishop Budge received a bachelor of arts degree in economics from BYU in 1984. He worked for Bain & Company Japan; Citibank, N.A.; and GE Capital in both Atlanta and Japan. In 2003 he became president and chief executive officer of Tokyo Star Bank Limited; from 2008 to 2011 he served as chairman of the board. He retired from the bank in 2011. Elder Joni L. Koch was sustained as a General Authority Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on April 1, 2017. At the time of his call, he had been serving as president of the Mozambique Maputo Mission. He previously served as Second Counselor in the Africa Southeast Area Presidency and President of the Brazil Area. He currently serves in the United States Northeast Area. Elder Koch received a Bachelor of Science degree in statistics from BYU in 1991. He received an executive MBA from FGV/SP in 1994. During his career he has worked in senior management positions at Cargill Foods, AP Moller Maersk Group, and was the CEO of CM Ltd. at the time of his call as mission president.

events.title: The Hebrew Bible's Ancient Avengers
events.description:
Long before Spider-Man, Wonder Woman, Batman and the Guardians of the Galaxy, the Hebrew Bible’s Ancient Avengers were inspiring Americans. Ripped from the story from ancient Israel, the figures of Samson, Esther, Elijah, and David served as spiritual sustenance to freedom fighters, politicians, and pundits striving to see the United States live up to its founding ideals. In this lecture we will examine how these Hebraic heroes shaped the American story from its founding era to today.

ABOUT THE SPEAKER

Rabbi Dr. Stuart Halpern serves as the senior advisor to the provost as well as the deputy director and chief strategy officer of the Zahava and Moshael J. Straus Center for Torah and Western Thought at Yeshiva University. In addition to his doctorate in education, Rabbi Halpern has master’s degrees in both Bible and Psychology in Education, and an MBA in Nonprofit Management.

events.title: Film Restoration Premiere—WHEN THOU ART CONVERTED
events.description:

We are happy to present this film for a new audience and restore the history of the work of the BYU Motion Picture Studio.

Starring Gordon Jump and Sherry Brian

November 20 7pm BYU Library Auditorium

Restoration premieres are a unique experience.

The restoration is seen for the first time, students and faculty present on the history of the film, and filmmakers and participants often attend to share their insight and experiences.

Please come celebrate these singular events!

events.title: Devotional: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
events.description:
Elder Gerrit W. Gong currently serves as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. He previously served as a member of the Asia Area Presidency and member of the Presidency of the Seventy.

During his 20 years in Washington, D.C., he served as special assistant to the undersecretary of state at the U.S. State Department, as special assistant to the U.S. ambassador in Beijing, China, and in several positions at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, D.C. He was also assistant to the president for planning and assessment at BYU.

Elder Gong holds a doctorate in international relations and a master’s degree in philosophy from Oxford University, where he was a Rhodes scholar. He also holds a bachelor's degree in Asian and university studies from BYU.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu
